# `liber:i2c-device@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:i2c-device` package (`i2c-device.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem I2C and SMBus - the contract an `i2c-bus` controller serves on one ADDRESS-SCOPED connection.  NEVER THE WHOLE BUS. The only connections to an `i2c-bus` provider are the ones DeviceManager mints with a SCOPED `CONNECT` naming one seven-bit address, so every operation below addresses that device and no other: there is no address argument to get wrong, and no way to reach a neighbour on the bus. The controller holds each address for one connection at a time.  ONE CONTRACT WITH A FUNCTIONALITY SET. A controller DECLARES the transactions it serves, and a consumer that needs one the controller lacks refuses it at bind instead of failing later: plain I2C - write, read, and a write then a read as ONE transfer with a repeated start, each at most `max-transfer` bytes - and the SMBus transactions, with the packet error code on any of them where the controller declares it. A transaction outside the declared set answers `unsupported`.  NO CLOCK RATE, NO BUS NUMBER AND NO PIN: a controller that has a clock takes it from its own firmware description. SMBus alert and host notify are not here; SMBus consumers poll.

### record `i2c-functionality`

What the controller serves.

| field | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plain` | `bool` | Write, read, and a write then a read with a repeated start. |

| `byte` | `bool` | Send byte and receive byte. |
| `byte-data` | `bool` | Read and write byte data. |
| `word-data` | `bool` | Read and write word data. |
| `block-write` | `bool` |  |
| `block-read` | `bool` | The block read whose length THE DEVICE sends first, at most 32 bytes. |
| `i2c-block-read` | `bool` | A read of a length the caller names, after a one-byte command. |
| `pec` | `bool` | The packet error code, on any declared SMBus transaction. |

### enum `i2c-status`

How a transfer ended on the bus.

| case | ordinal | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ok` | 0 |  |
| `no-device` | 1 | Nothing answered at the address. |
| `interrupted` | 2 | The transfer did not complete - the device stopped acknowledging, or the controller says only that it failed. |
| `too-long` | 3 | Longer than the controller's bound. |
| `controller` | 4 | The controller itself failed. |
| `unsupported` | 5 | Outside the declared functionality set. |
| `pec` | 6 | The packet error code the device sent does not match its bytes. |

### record `i2c-reply`

A transfer's status and what it read: the bytes of a read, a byte for a byte and two for a word (low byte first), the block for a block read. Empty for a write.

| field | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `i2c-status` |  |
| `bytes` | `list<u8>` |  |
